messages:
anya: quick heads-up — brought up quantized reranker v2 (int8 hybrid) on holdout. ndcg is up ~0.8% but mrr dropped ~1.9% across 3 holdout splits. smallish N but consistent. anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: yikes. did we change candidate ordering or tie-breaking during offline eval? that can hit mrr.

mike: offline harness command used:
```
./eval_rerank --model build/v2-int8 --candidates holdout.tsv --preserve_order=false --metric ndcg,mrr --seed=42
```
we forgot to set --preserve_order=true for parity with prod.

anya: ah — good catch. prod inference preserves candidate order. can that explain ndcg up / mrr down?

kevin: yes, ndcg is less sensitive to top-1 swaps than mrr. if ordering changes around the top, mrr moves more. also quantization can change score magnitudes that affect tie-breaks.

sam: also check tokenizer and priming differences. we recently switched to the new tokenizer fastbp. tokenization shift + quant noise = weird rank deltas.

mike: reproduced quickly with preserve_order=true: mrr drop reduces to ~0.4% (almost within noise), ndcg still +0.6%. so ordering accounted for most of it.

anya: thanks. still a ~0.4% mrr gap — doing a quick ablation to isolate quant vs tokenization.

ci-bot: triggered CI job 1795554322-quant-ablation (owner: eva).

eva: running three ablations: (A) float32 vs int8 (same tokenizer, same order), (B) int8 with old tokenizer, (C) int8 with new tokenizer + preserve_order. ETA ~25m.

kevin: also pull logs for KV-cache/batching differences. different batching heuristics can change effective context length and lead to small score shifts.

mike: noted. my quick smoke shows float32 vs int8 (preserve_order=true, tokenizer=fastbp) => mrr delta -0.38%, ndcg +0.5%.

sam: ok that's reproducible. next step: check score distribution shift. can you dump top-5 scores for a sample of queries (float vs int)?

mike: pasted sample:
```
query_id: 1234
float_scores: [2.34, 1.88, 1.12, 0.05, -0.22]
int8_scores:  [2.31, 1.90, 1.10, 0.01, -0.30]
```
looks like small compression at tails and slightly different tie orders.

anya: thanks. action items: 1) keep preserve_order=true in eval by default (mike to update harness), 2) add a small calibration step for score rescaling after quant (eva), 3) add a short doc note about tokenizer parity for bring-ups (anya).

eva: for calibration idea — we can fit a simple affine rescale on a small dev partition to match float score mean/variance before computing mrr/ndcg. low-risk.

kevin: can we automate that as an optional postprocess in the eval harness (flag --calibrate-quant)?

mike: yep I can add flag and a reproducible notebook for the calibration fit.

sam: also let's add a small regression test that checks top1 stability for a tiny golden set (10 queries) — fail fast if top1 flips > 2 queries after quant. keeps oncall sane. :thumbsup:

anya: agreed. i've created a follow-up ticket and assigned owners. will post results from eva's calibration run when ready. thanks team.

ci-bot: job 1795554322-quant-ablation succeeded. artifacts: /artifacts/1795554322/ablation-report.html

mike: calibration reduced mrr gap to ~0.07% on dev-preview. pushing PR for harness and --calibrate-quant.

eva: PR reviewed, test added, and short run of goldenset passes. merging shortly. :tada:

anya: great. summary for later: initial ndcg up + mrr down traced to candidate-order parity + quant score compression. solved by preserving order + optional affine calibration + goldenset sanity test. documenting now.

sam: nice triage. closing thread.
